description:
Connection to one Stalwart server (v0.16). Cluster-scoped: an org-wide
piece of infrastructure, not owned by a namespace (a namespace's own
server is a `StalwartLocalInstance`). `Ready` tells whether the server
answers with the token below and speaks a management schema this
operator release supports.

appPasswordTokenSecretRef.description:
A second API key of Stalwart, on the same account as the one above:
the one that creates, rotates and revokes the App Passwords of the
`StalwartServiceAccount`s (permissions `authenticate`,
`impersonate`, `emailSend` and `sysAppPassword*` only). Read on
every reconcile of a `StalwartServiceAccount`; unset, those fail
with `TokenSecretMissing` (the other kinds don't use it).

secretStore.description:
Default destination of the secrets the CRs bound to this instance
emit, when they list no `secretTargets`. Default: a Kubernetes
`Secret`.

backend.description:
Backend of a CR's implicit target (one named after the CR, when it
lists no `secretTargets`).

vault.description: The Vault connection a `vault` target writes through.

caSecretRef.description:
A private CA to verify Vault's TLS with: a PEM bundle under `key`
of a `Secret`, read through the API. Unset: the system trust store.
Only consulted for `https://` addresses.

kubernetesAuthMount.description: Mount path of Vault's Kubernetes auth backend.

kubernetesAuthRole.description:
Vault Kubernetes-auth role the operator authenticates as: its own
ServiceAccount token is exchanged for a Vault token through
`auth/<kubernetesAuthMount>/login`.

mount.description:
KV v2 secrets engine mount (e.g. `secret`) credentials are written
under.

pathGrants.description:
Vault paths this instance's CRs may write to outside their
namespace's subtree `<pathPrefix>/<namespace>/`, per namespace
(`clusterScoped` is refused: every object writing credentials is
namespaced). The Vault policy of the operator's role stays the hard
bound.

items.description:
Paths of the instance's secret backend that objects may write to
outside their namespace's subtree `<pathPrefix>/<namespace>/`. Opens
them to every subject allowed to create an emitting object in a
covered namespace, and cannot hand over a value another object owns.

clusterScoped.description:
The grant opens `paths` to cluster-scoped objects (instead of
`namespaces`).

namespaces.description:
Namespaces whose objects may write `paths`: exact names, `*`, or a
prefix glob such as `team-*`. `team-*` opens the paths to every
matching namespace.

paths.description:
Path patterns under the mount, compared segment by segment: a
literal segment matches itself, `+` exactly one segment, and a last
`*` one or more. Each holds at least one literal segment, e.g.
`shared/auth`, `+/auth`, `platform/*`. Prefer exact paths where
values not written by the operator live: a covered object may take
over a value no object owns yet.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: a path pattern has no "." or ".." segment
a path pattern has at least one literal segment
a grant names namespaces or is clusterScoped, not both

pathPrefix.description:
Path prefix under `mount`: the default KV path of a target is
`<pathPrefix>/<namespace>/<name>`, one secret per target. Empty:
`<namespace>/<name>`. An explicit `path` must stay under
`<pathPrefix>/<namespace>/` unless `pathGrants` opens it.

With an empty prefix, a path holding a value no CR owns (written by
another tool) is taken over by the first CR writing it: only the
Vault policy of the operator's role then keeps a CR away from such
values. Keep a prefix unless that policy is narrowed to the paths
the CRs may write.

x-kubernetes-validations.message: pathGrants name namespaces: every object writing credentials is namespaced, clusterScoped grants never apply

submission.description: The submission service the emitted credentials announce.

host.description: Host name of the submission service.

security.description: Transport security a client must use.

tls.description:
TLS verification of the connection above: a private CA to trust
(`tls.caSecretRef`), or `tls.insecureSkipVerify`. Default: the
platform trust store.

caSecretRef.description:
Optional custom CA certificate to verify the instance's TLS with,
read from a Kubernetes `Secret` (the referenced `key` must hold a PEM
bundle). Use this to trust a private CA without mounting it into the
operator pod — the operator reads the Secret via the API and hands the
PEM to its HTTP client. It is added *on top of* the platform trust
store, so publicly-signed endpoints keep working. When unset, only the
platform trust store (plus the usual `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR`
env vars) is used.

insecureSkipVerify.description:
Skip certificate verification entirely — insecure, intended only for
throwaway/self-signed instances. Prefer `caSecretRef` below, which
trusts a private CA without turning verification off.

tokenSecretRef.description:
An API key of Stalwart, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Read on
every reconcile: rotating it needs no restart.

url.description:
Base URL of the Stalwart HTTP listener, e.g.
`http://stalwart.mail.svc:8080`. Management goes through JMAP,
`POST <url>/jmap` (session `GET <url>/jmap/session`); `<url>/api`
only serves the schema, whose hash identifies the server's version.
